```{r}
library(knitr)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "—")

read_if <- function(path) if (file.exists(path)) read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE) else data.frame()
fig <- function(name, caption = NULL) {
  path <- file.path("mfclshiny", "figures", paste0(name, ".png"))
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(invisible(NULL))
  knitr::include_graphics(path)
}

management <- read_if(file.path("tables", "management-quantities.csv"))
fit <- read_if(file.path("tables", "fit-summary.csv"))
hessian <- read_if(file.path("tables", "hessian-summary.csv"))
age_fit <- read_if(file.path("mfclshiny", "tables", "age-data-fit-summary.csv"))
age_fit_region <- read_if(file.path("mfclshiny", "tables", "age-data-fit-by-region-summary.csv"))
growth_parameters <- read_if(file.path("tables", "growth-parameter-uncertainty.csv"))
```

## Assessment summary

The Diagnostic model converged with a positive-definite 1,997-parameter Hessian. The report combines the fitted-model diagnostics with native MFCL delta-method uncertainty. Uncertainty ribbons and intervals are pointwise 95% confidence intervals conditional on this model specification.

```{r}
if (nrow(fit)) {
  fit_view <- data.frame(
    Metric = c("Objective function", "Maximum gradient", "Dynamic 2024 depletion", "Fit status"),
    Value = c(
      format(fit$objective[[1]], digits = 10, scientific = FALSE),
      format(fit$max_gradient[[1]], digits = 4, scientific = TRUE),
      format(fit$terminal_depletion_2024[[1]], digits = 4),
      fit$status[[1]]
    )
  )
  kable(fit_view, align = c("l", "r"))
}
```

## Stock status and uncertainty

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Hessian-based uncertainty for dynamic spawning depletion, spawning potential and quarterly recruitment. Ribbons are pointwise 95% delta-method intervals."
knitr::include_graphics(file.path("figures", "hessian-time-series.png"))
```

The management quantities use the averaging windows implemented by the current MFCL source for this fitted model: `SBrecent` is 2021 Q1–2024 Q4, `Frecent` is 2020 Q1–2023 Q4, and the no-fishing spawning-potential denominator is 2014 Q1–2023 Q4. These definitions are intentionally separate from the dynamic quarterly depletion series.

```{r}
if (nrow(management)) {
  management_view <- transform(
    management[c("quantity", "definition", "averaging_period", "estimate", "lower_95", "upper_95", "note")],
    estimate = format(estimate, digits = 4),
    lower_95 = format(lower_95, digits = 4),
    upper_95 = format(upper_95, digits = 4)
  )
  names(management_view) <- c("Quantity", "Definition", "Period", "Estimate", "Lower 95%", "Upper 95%", "Note")
  kable(management_view, align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "l"))
}
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Recent fishing intensity and spawning-biomass status relative to MSY reference points. Error bars are pointwise 95% delta-method intervals."
knitr::include_graphics(file.path("figures", "management-status-uncertainty.png"))
```

## Size and age composition

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Observed regional age–length cells and the common fitted growth schedule; the final panel pools all regions. The blue band is the pointwise 95% confidence interval for mean length-at-age. The orange band is the fitted mean ± 1.96 SD length-at-age distribution, and the dark boundary ribbons propagate Hessian uncertainty in both distribution limits. The lower panels show the corresponding 95% CI half-widths without visual magnification."
knitr::include_graphics(file.path("figures", "regional-age-length-growth-uncertainty.png"))
```

```{r}
if (nrow(growth_parameters)) {
  growth_view <- growth_parameters[c("parameter", "estimate", "standard_error", "lower_95", "upper_95")]
  growth_view[-1] <- lapply(growth_view[-1], function(x) format(x, digits = 4))
  names(growth_view) <- c("Parameter", "Estimate", "SE", "Lower 95%", "Upper 95%")
  kable(growth_view, caption = "Growth and length-at-age SD parameters with bounded-scale Hessian intervals.")
}
```

The fitted growth schedule is shared among regions; regional panels differ only in their observed age–length data. Growth intervals are multivariate Hessian intervals generated on MFCL's bounded internal parameter scale and transformed through the native sine bounds. They are not lognormal intervals. The boundary ribbons quantify uncertainty in the fitted distribution limits, not additional biological variation beyond the central orange distribution.

```{r}
if (nrow(age_fit)) {
  kable(head(age_fit, 30), caption = "Conditional age-at-length fit summary. The complete fishery and regional tables are supplied as CSV with the report.")
}
if (nrow(age_fit_region)) {
  regional_summary <- age_fit_region[order(age_fit_region$conditional_rmse, decreasing = TRUE), ]
  regional_summary$conditional_rmse <- round(regional_summary$conditional_rmse, 4)
  regional_summary$conditional_mae <- round(regional_summary$conditional_mae, 4)
  names(regional_summary) <- c(
    "Region", "Fish aged", "Fitted fish", "Observed age-length cells",
    "Conditional RMSE", "Conditional MAE"
  )
  kable(regional_summary, caption = "Regional conditional age-at-length misfit, ordered by observed-versus-fitted conditional-proportion RMSE.")
}
```

## Hessian quality control

```{r}
if (nrow(hessian)) kable(hessian, col.names = c("Diagnostic", "Value"), align = c("l", "r"))
```

All 1,997 eigenvalues are positive. The condition number indicates substantial scale variation, so intervals should be interpreted as local, model-conditional approximations. The MSY point estimate is retained, but an interval is not shown because the native intermediate derivative mode returned a zero derivative for MSY; this is not evidence of zero uncertainty.

## Reproducibility and definitions

The report is generated from the archived final PAR, matching 70-part Hessian, raw MFCL fit files, and compact payload. `diagnostic-uncertainty.rds` and the CSV files under `tables/` retain the plotted values. The companion offline viewer under `mfclshiny/interactive-model-viewer.html` exposes the complete model plotting set.

Dynamic depletion is `SB(t)/SB(F=0,t)`. The management terminal and recent depletion ratios instead divide by the mean no-fishing spawning potential over 2014–2023. Keeping these definitions separate avoids the small but important difference between the dynamic 2024 value and the management terminal value.
